title: VI. Notable points on original sin: imputation, propagation, and extent
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): Fifth, baptism plus regeneration do not remove all corruption in this life, but ye guilt plus dominion belonging toward sin (Romans 6-7). Fourth, it does not take away free choice as to natural acts, but deprives belonging toward powers toward spiritual good. Third, original sin stands as not a substance, but a privative accident plus a positive habit belonging toward evil. Second, propagation happens through natural generation, not through creation belonging toward ye soul as sinful by means belonging toward God. First, Adams sin stands as imputed to posterity not by means belonging toward imitation alone, but by means belonging toward a real communication belonging toward guilt, because all were in Adam as in a head plus root (Romans 5:12). Certain points stand as here to be NOTED. VI.
pass_b_english: VI. Certain points are here to be NOTED. First, Adams sin is imputed to posterity not by imitation alone, but by a real communication of guilt, because all were in Adam as in a head and root (Romans 5:12). Second, propagation happens through natural generation, not through creation of the soul as sinful by God. Third, original sin is not a substance, but a privative accident and a positive habit of evil. Fourth, it does not take away free choice as to natural acts, but deprives of powers toward spiritual good. Fifth, baptism and regeneration do not remove all corruption in this life, but the guilt and dominion of sin (Romans 6-7).
source_text: VI. Sunt autem hic quaedam NOTANDA. 1. Peccatum Adami imputatur posteris non sola imitatione, sed reali communicatione reatus, quia omnes in Adamo tanquam in capite et radice fuerunt (Rom. 5:12). 2. Propagatio fit per generationem naturalem, non per creationem animae tanquam peccatricis a Deo. 3. Peccatum originale non est substantia, sed accidens privativum et positivum habitus mali. 4. Non tollit liberum arbitrium quoad actus naturales, sed privat viribus ad bonum spirituale. 5. Baptismus et regeneratio non auferunt totam corruptionem in hac vita, sed reatum et dominationem peccati (Rom. 6-7).
